text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Not ready for final diagnosis yet; the 1-week onset of right leg weakness and unsteady gait, combined with 6 months of cognitive decline and paranoia, suggests a rapidly progressive neurodegenerative disorder such as Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease or an acute structural lesion like a brainstem stroke or tumor. I need to confirm if there are any episodes of visual hallucinations, myoclonus (muscle jerks), or if the memory loss was preceded by personality changes. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with and without contrast.
